items.title: Roswell Rudd interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: Because I had a friend like Steve Lacy... While at Yale, Roswell performed Dixieland music with Eli’s Chosen Six and shortly after started an association with saxophonist Steve Lacy.

ctx.x: You have to have some intense longing for the music to pay those kind of dues.

Yeah, I knew — and the thing was, Monk, I knew that I was behind. I knew that somehow that spending those four years in college and maybe the high school before that, I felt somehow that I should have been doing this a lot sooner, and doing it just as intensely but a lot sooner. So it took me longer than I wanted to get there. So once I got there I felt like I really had a lot to do in a short period of time to be able to catch up to what was happening. Because I had a friend like Steve Lacy who grew up in New…
Well do you think it’s — your name is certainly a part of the circle of musicians at that time in the ‘60s and so forth that was known as “free jazz.” Do you think that’s a correct term?
